title: Data Quality and Fitness for Use
summary: Assess whether a defined dataset can support a specific analytical or control purpose, with record-level defects and explicit release restrictions.
audience: Data stewards, control analysts, and review teams
decision: Is the supplied dataset sufficiently supported for the stated use, and which defects require human resolution?
report_sections: Limitations quality review and human disposition

findings.title: Critical validity and completeness defects prevent an unrestricted recommendation
findings.detail: D02 has a blank name and impossible date; D03 has a code outside the fictional approved set.
findings.recommendation: Propose restricted use pending source-owner correction and record-level retest.

findings.title: Duplicated customer key affects two supplied records
findings.detail: P005 appears on D05 and D06 where the contract requires one row per customer. Two affected rows form one duplicate group and one excess row.
findings.recommendation: Resolve source lineage before any merge or removal; reconcile corrected counts.

findings.title: One refresh date exceeds the illustrative freshness horizon
findings.detail: D03 is 730 days old at 2026-09-30 against a 365-day illustration.
findings.recommendation: Obtain current evidence or document a permitted limitation for the intended use.

limitations: The allowed codes and 365-day horizon are fictional contractual examples.
The check inventory cannot detect every possible data defect.
Duplicate keys establish a contract breach, not authority to merge records.
No source-system correction or feed restriction was executed.
conclusion: Four of six fictional records are affected by critical defects, so the evidence supports a restricted-use recommendation. The 79.3% diagnostic check-pass rate cannot override critical gates; correction and acceptance remain human decisions.
report_narrative: Four of six fictional records are affected by critical defects. The draft recommendation is restricted use pending source-confirmed correction and human acceptance; a 79.3% diagnostic check-pass rate cannot override the critical gates.

The extract has six active rows, five distinct customer keys, and a one-row-per-customer contract. The fixture uses five rules, a limited US/CA/GB code set, and a 365-day freshness horizon; these are illustrative contractual choices.

D02 has a blank name and impossible birth date; D03 has an unapproved code and stale refresh date; D05 and D06 share the same customer key. Duplicate keys breach this contract but do not authorize a merge or deletion.

DataRecords preserves all six original rows, including nulls and invalid date text. There are no exclusions. The key P005 forms one duplicate group, two affected rows, and one excess row; these counts describe different aspects of the defect.

Rule eligibility totals 6 + 6 + 5 + 6 + 6 = 29 checks; six fail and 23 pass. The ENTITY row D04 is outside the individual birth-date denominator. Critical affected IDs are the distinct union D02, D03, D05, D06, or 4/6 = 66.7%.

SYN-001 supports the record-level arithmetic and rule outcomes. The public BCBS sources provide method context only; they do not prescribe the fictional code list, freshness horizon, or zero-failure gates. Upstream real-world accuracy is outside this fixture.

Propose source-owner correction for D02 and D03, lineage resolution for P005, and current refresh evidence. Retest the corrected extract and reconcile any approved removal to the original six records; do not improve rates by silently dropping defects.

QA checks calendar validity, conditional eligibility, duplicate accounting, and distinct affected-row totals. Actual feed acceptance, source correction, or use restrictions require an authorized human decision; no production action occurred.
